A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MSGNav research, and their text, equations, tables and figures are readable. The supplied v1 ends after the references; v3 includes supplementary Sections 6–9. Retained content can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original navigation evaluations, component ablations, scene-graph comparisons and viewpoint analyses in Tables 1–5 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v3 retains original navigation experiments and adds HM3D-ObjNav results, VLM-backbone comparisons and qualitative navigation analyses, including supplementary results.

M1.justification: The graph construction, greedy subgraph selection, vocabulary updates, decision memory and visibility-based viewpoint selection remain unchanged in Equations 1–7 and Algorithms 1–2. The supplement supplies prompts and verification details without establishing a procedural redesign. Explicitly listing the already-used obstruction parameter in Algorithm 2 is documentation.

E1.justification: v3 adds the Habitat 2022 HM3D-ObjNav object-navigation benchmark beyond the previously evaluated multimodal lifelong GOAT-Bench and open-vocabulary HM3D-OVON tasks. HM3D-OVON remains separately reported in supplementary Table 9, confirming that ObjNav is additional coverage rather than a renamed benchmark.

E2.justification: The new HM3D-ObjNav comparison introduces a substantially different comparator set, including ProcTHOR-ZS, ZSON, PSL, L3MVN, Trihelper and Apexnav. In the corresponding HM3D-OVON comparison, BC and TANGO disappear between v1 Table 1 and v3 Table 9. GOAT-Bench comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: HM3D-OVON changes from the explicitly stated Val Unseen evaluation in v1 Section 4.1/Table 1 to Val Seen in v3 Section 7.1/Table 9. MSGNav's scores remain identical, so this establishes a reported protocol revision, not whether experiments were rerun. GOAT-Bench's Val Unseen evaluation, SR/SPL metrics and first-episode ablation design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 supplies the previously unavailable GPT-4o versus Qwen-VL-Max comparison and adds viewpoint-visibility, exploration and visual-grounding case studies in Sections 7.2–8 and Figures 7–11. These extend analysis to backbone dependence and illustrated reasoning behavior. The original component, graph-representation and success-threshold ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. The distance–visibility boxplot in Figure 5 is retained unchanged; the new tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds HM3D-ObjNav results of 63.0 SR/31.4 SPL and Qwen-VL-Max GOAT-Bench results of 52.79/30.79, plus modality breakdowns. Under the revised OVON split, MTU3D changes from 40.8/12.1 to 55.0/23.6 and overtakes MSGNav in SR; MSGNav remains 48.3/27.0. These are not same-setting performance gains. GOAT-Bench totals and Tables 3–5 remain unchanged. The isolated CLR accuracy claim of 43.8% to 64.8% is removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical graph definitions, update equations, greedy selection and visibility calculations are retained. Section 8.1 explains Algorithm 2 step by step but introduces no new derivation, formal assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list replace the claimed HM3D-OVON state-of-the-art result with HM3D-ObjNav. The previous claim of leading both SR and SPL on unseen OVON environments becomes a supplementary claim of leading SPL on the seen split, with MTU3D higher in SR. The central M3DSG and last-mile methodological contributions remain unchanged; the conclusion still names OVON.

C2.justification: v3 reinterprets OVON results as within-distribution navigation efficiency rather than direct unseen-environment generalization. It adds a visibility-versus-path-length explanation for the ObjNav SPL deficit, expands the AVU/CLR complementarity explanation, and discusses Qwen-oriented prompt development. The conclusion removes the reinforcement-learning future-work suggestion, while Section 4.3.3 retains the qualification that VVD does not eliminate the last-mile problem.

D1.justification: Sections 6 and 9 newly disclose GPU/VRAM requirements, VFM versions, viewpoint radii, sampling and adjacency parameters, camera/image settings, and four actual prompt templates. Table 8 supplies evaluation sample counts. These materially expand implementation documentation. Conversely, v1's precise Qwen-VL-Max version date is omitted in v3; the code link and future-release statement remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: References add works supporting the ObjNav comparisons, including GOAT, ProcTHOR, ZSON, PSL, L3MVN, Trihelper and Apexnav, and replace the unrelated OpenFMNav citation with the named OpenFMNav work. Several background references disappear. The two related-work subsections and the positioning around visual scene graphs and zero-shot navigation remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: v3 substantially expands exposition through an explanatory supplement, including a step-by-step account of the existing VVD algorithm and structured explanations of exploration and VLM prompting. It also reorders and rewrites the benchmark discussion and edits prose throughout the main text. The underlying methodological section organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is rearranged into a single row and drops the OVON scatterplot. GOAT-Bench moves from Table 2 to Table 1, while the revised OVON comparison moves to supplementary Table 9 and ObjNav occupies Table 2. New parameter/model tables, backbone results, perception and navigation visualizations, and full-page prompt panels substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The added settings, model details, prompts and diagnostic examples substantially improve transparency relative to v1. However, the principal OVON result of 48.3/27.0 is reassigned from Val Unseen to Val Seen without explaining its provenance, while baseline scores, rankings and benchmark claims change. The PDFs do not establish whether this corrects earlier reporting or reflects a different evaluation. That unresolved experimental revision prevents a reliable net judgment despite clear documentation gains.
